## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Shīzǐ zhuāngyán wáng púsà qǐngwèn jīng* (T486) is a one-fascicle Mahāyāna sūtra translated by the Tang Indian monk [那提](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%A3%E6%8F%90) Nàtí — a transliteration that may render Sanskrit *Punyodaya* (Puṇyodaya) or *Nadī*. The bodhisattva *Shīzǐ zhuāngyán wáng* 師子莊嚴王 ("Lion-Adornment-King"; Sanskrit *Siṃhālaṃkāra-rāja*) is the principal interlocutor.

**Abstract**

Nàtí (also written 布如烏伐邪 / 福生) was a sixth- to seventh-century Indian monk who arrived in Cháng'ān in 655 CE bringing 1,500 Indic texts. He worked at the Cíēn sì 慈恩寺 alongside [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) Xuánzàng's translation institute but was sent on a mission to South Asia (663 CE) by the Tang court to gather rare medicinal plants. He translated only a small number of texts before his departure; this one-fascicle bodhisattva-question sūtra is one of his three surviving Chinese translations (with *Lígòuhuì púsà suǒwèn lǐfó fǎ jīng* [KR6i0116](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0116) and one other).

The translation date is 663 CE per the *Kāiyuán shìjiào lù*.
